advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Strengthen the explicit-empty-project preview check so it asserts the ticket's own plan entry is absent/unrouted rather than relying on a vacuously-true empty-set subset assertion.
evidence: _assert_scope body: `assert planned <= intended` and `stray = planned & others; assert not stray` — both hold trivially when `planned` is empty

The module docstring claims the empty-intersection assertion is what SURFACES a stray target in preview; for an empty-scope expectation there is nothing to surface, so the claim does not hold for scenario 3's preview step.
advisory.finding: The `_assert_scope(preview, set(), work)` gate in the explicit-empty-project scenario is vacuously satisfied: when `_planned_projects(preview)` is empty, both `planned <= intended` and `planned & others` pass regardless of WHY the plan is empty. So this preview assertion cannot distinguish 'the not-synced ticket was correctly excluded' from 'the preview produced no plan at all (e.g. the store failed to see the ticket)'. The real regression-catcher is only the post-sync `_keys_by_label` check.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-target scenario 9 so the injected fault forces the harness/bridge cleanup seam (e.g. session teardown sweep or per-scenario finally under the real fixture) to run, rather than proving the test's own finally.
evidence: Docstring claims 'Prove per-issue cleanup runs even when the scenario body raises mid-flight' but the finally block that does the deleting is written in the same test — the recovery under test is test-local, not a production contract. Litmus (unrealistic fault injection): the fault is injected OUTSIDE any cleanup seam, so the seam's recovery code never runs.
advisory.finding: The 'failure-path cleanup proof' (scenario 9) injects a synthetic _InjectedScenarioFailure directly in the test body and the 'cleanup' it proves is the test's OWN try/finally deleting the probe — no rebar/bridge cleanup seam is exercised. The injected fault does not force any production recovery path to run, so the test cannot detect a regression in the harness's actual cleanup contract (the session-teardown sweep or any bridge-side per-issue cleanup).
scenarios: A regression that breaks the session-teardown sweep or any bridge cleanup seam would still leave this test green, since it only proves its own finally executes.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In scenario 1, assert the inbound-created local ticket's source project and repos from the ingest result, not from the seeded bridge_projects_list mapping.
evidence: "assert mapping[REB_PROJECT][\"repos\"] == [\"rebar\"], \"REB ingested with the wrong repo list\""

The only ingest-observing assertion is `{REB_PROJECT, DIG_PROJECT} <= planned` on the sync plan; no assertion inspects a created local ticket's source project / repos, so an ingest that dropped repos or mis-sourced would not be caught by the repo-list checks (they assert the seed, unchanged).
advisory.finding: Scenario 1 (test_inbound_from_both_projects) claims to verify that each probe ingested 'sourced from its own project with that project's configured repos', but the repo-list assertions read rebar.bridge_projects_list — i.e. the mapping the rehearsal_store fixture just seeded — rather than any local ticket actually produced by the inbound ingest. The repo assertions re-check fixture setup, not ingest behavior.
scenarios: An inbound-ingest regression that mis-attributes source project or repo list would pass because the assertion reads the seeded mapping, not the ingested ticket.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `_planned_projects` (or `_assert_scope`) fail loudly on a create plan entry that carries neither a Jira-key target nor a `_bridge_target_project` stamp, instead of silently contributing nothing.
evidence: test_multi_project_rehearsal.py: `stamped = (entry.get("fields") or {}).get(_BRIDGE_TARGET_PROJECT); if stamped: projects.add(stamped)` — a missing stamp is silently skipped ('Nones are skipped')

src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py:598-601: `canonical = next((k ...), None); if canonical is None: return` — the create path can emit a mutation WITHOUT the `_bridge_target_project` stamp
src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/run_differs.py:515-522: create target is `om.local_id` (never a Jira key), so the regex branch never applies to creates — the stamp is the only signal.
dropped.finding: `_planned_projects` extracts a project for a CREATE only from `fields[_bridge_target_project]`, but if the differ ever fails to stamp that key (e.g. an unmapped target, per outbound_differ where `canonical is None` returns without stamping), the create entry contributes NOTHING to the planned set. Combined with the subset-based `_assert_scope`, an unstamped-but-actually-routed create would read as 'no project planned' and pass the scope gate silently.
